answer: Because the beacon calculation reruns each epoch, the tundra weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the juniper settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 151 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 51% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 24 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
